claim: The PR says `auto` (autoApprove) now matches --arx/--drx case-insensitively, but no test checks this: reverting auth_cli.dart:1080 and :1083 to `RegExp(arx)`/`RegExp(drx)` keeps every test green, even though `auto -A wavi` would then ignore a request named `Wavi` again.
mechanism: autoApprove builds its own regexes at auth_cli.dart:1079-1084 and matches each announced request with them at :1107-1108, falling to the 'Ignoring enrollment request which does not match the regex filters' branch at :1136. That code does not go through `_list`. All four new tests in auth_cli_list_test.dart (lines 68-174) call only `auth_cli.list`, which reaches `_list` at auth_cli.dart:911-912 and never this listener. The only tests that drive autoApprove are 'auto_approve' (auth_cli_approve_test.dart:124) and the revoked-via-auto_approve test (:168), both through `autoApproveB()`. That helper parses `--arx wavi --drx phone` (:95-102) and announces a notification whose payload is `{'appName': 'wavi', 'deviceName': 'phone'}` (:94). Pattern and name are both lower case, so `RegExp('wavi').hasMatch('wavi')` is true with or without `caseSensitive: false`. approvals == [b] holds and both tests pass after the revert. The functional tests (tests/at_onboarding_cli_functional_tests/test/enrollment_cli_commands_test.dart) approve, revoke and unrevoke by `-i <enrollmentId>`, never `-A`/`-D` or `auto`. The PR description admits the gap. A test would be cheap: the `autoApproveB` harness already exists and would only need a mixed-case payload such as `{'appName': 'Wavi', ...}`.
repro: Change auth_cli.dart:1080 to `appRegex = RegExp(arx);` and :1083 to `deviceRegex = RegExp(drx);`, then run `dart test` in packages/at_onboarding_cli. All tests still pass, including the new auth_cli_list_test.dart cases and both auto_approve tests in auth_cli_approve_test.dart. In use, `at_activate auto -a @alice -A wavi -D phone` with a new request whose appName is "Wavi" prints 'Ignoring enrollment request which does not match the regex filters' and keeps waiting. `at_activate approve -A wavi` still approves the same request, because it goes through `_list`.

v.reason: The mechanism traced in the source confirms the claim. autoApprove compiles its own regexes at auth_cli.dart:1080/:1083 (caseSensitive: false) and matches decoded notification payloads with them at :1107-1108, falling to the 'Ignoring enrollment request' branch at :1136 — this listener never routes through _list, whose separate case-insensitive regexes live at :911-912. All new tests in auth_cli_list_test.dart (four tests starting at lines 68, 103, 136, 156 within the claimed 68-174 range) call only auth_cli.list, i.e. _list. The only tests that exercise autoApprove are 'auto_approve' (auth_cli_approve_test.dart:124) and the revoked-via-auto_approve test (:168), both via autoApproveB(), whose payload is {'appName': 'wavi', 'deviceName': 'phone'} (:94) and whose --arx/--drx values are 'wavi'/'phone' (:95-102). Since RegExp('wavi').hasMatch('wavi') is true regardless of caseSensitive, reverting :1080/:1083 to RegExp(arx)/RegExp(drx) keeps both auto_approve tests green, and the list tests never touch this code. No guard or other test prevents the gap. One citation could not be verified: the functional test file packages/at_onboarding_cli/test/at_onboarding_cli_functional_tests/test/enrollment_cli_commands_test.dart does not exist (repeated reads failed with not-found), so I could not check the -i/-A/-D usage it describes; however, that file's absence only weakens the pool of tests that could have covered the auto path — it cannot refute the coverage gap established by the unit tests.

claim: Case-insensitive regex matching for --arx and --drx in autoApprove is not verified by any test, allowing regressions back to case-sensitive matching to pass undetected.
mechanism: The PR updates autoApprove (auth_cli.dart:1080, 1083) to compile arx and drx with RegExp(..., caseSensitive: false) so incoming enrollment requests can be matched and approved case-insensitively at lines 1107-1108. However, all new tests were added to auth_cli_list_test.dart for the list command. The only existing test exercising autoApprove is in auth_cli_approve_test.dart (autoApproveB, line 80), which constructs both the notification payload ({'appName': 'wavi', 'deviceName': 'phone'}) and the CLI options (--arx wavi --drx phone) using identical all-lowercase strings. If caseSensitive: false is removed from lines 1080 and 1083, the case-sensitive RegExp still matches the identical-case notification payload, so every test in the suite continues to pass.
repro: Revert lines 1080 and 1083 of packages/at_onboarding_cli/lib/src/cli/auth_cli.dart to RegExp(arx) and RegExp(drx). Run dart test; all tests pass, but at_activate auto with --arx wavi fails to match incoming enrollment notifications with appName "Wavi", silently ignoring rather than approving them.

v.reason: The claim holds in every traced detail. autoApprove (auth_cli.dart:1080,1083) compiles arx/drx with caseSensitive: false and matches incoming notification payload fields at 1107-1108. The only test exercising autoApprove is autoApproveB (auth_cli_approve_test.dart:80), and both the notification payload ('appName': 'wavi', 'deviceName': 'phone', line 94) and the parsed CLI options (--arx wavi --drx phone, lines 98-101) use identical all-lowercase strings, so a case-sensitive RegExp would still match. The mixed-case coverage in auth_cli_list_test.dart:68-101 targets the `list` command, whose filtering runs through _list (auth_cli.dart:911-912), which compiles its own RegExp objects independently of autoApprove's — so those tests cannot detect removal of caseSensitive: false at 1080/1083. No other autoApprove test exists (probe reads of auth_cli_approve_multi_test.dart and auth_cli_auto_approve_case_test.dart both failed with not-found; the remaining at_onboarding_cli_test.dart tests the onboarding service, not autoApprove). Thus a regression back to case-sensitive matching in autoApprove would pass the whole suite undetected, exactly as claimed.
